chapter: Mambo, the Palladium and Cubop City
title: Live-audience recording at the church on 30th Street
summary: For "Frisilandia" and "Zambia" they brought seventy or eighty high-school kids and Palladium regulars to give audience atmosphere.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Okay, there came a time where, I think it was 1951 or fifty - fifty one, you recorded "Frisilandia", "Zambia" and all of them.
I understand there was a little gimmick that you used to get people in the studio. Do you remember what the gimmick was?
Well, we wanted to create the atmosphere for the band and for the public and live recording, so actually all these kids from high school they was there, and ....
But how did you get them there?'

Well, listen, we start to record about four so we brought them from practically every high school around and besides, the people that used to go to the Palladium, all those too, so everybody was there. We had about seventy or eighty, it was a big ....
That's right because I hear like an audience response in "Biribicumbi", it's like a -- I thought that was done in another time and that. That was done there in the ......
At the 30th St. between 3rd. Ave. and 2nd Ave., that big church.
